title: Practical: Math Library
story: You keep rewriting `is_prime`, `factorial`, and `gcd` in every program. Time to build a proper math module - organize them, add contracts for safety, and never rewrite them again.
why: A reusable math module with contracts ensures your numeric functions are correct, fast, and available everywhere with a simple `use` statement.
analogy: A workshop has labeled drawers: 'screwdrivers', 'hammers', 'wrenches'. Each tool has a safety label (contract) showing proper use. The math module is your labeled, safety-checked drawer of numeric tools.
try_it: Add `lcm(a, b)` (least common multiple) using the formula: `lcm(a,b) = (a * b) / gcd(a,b)`. Add `is_even(n)` and `is_odd(n)` helpers. Try calling `factorial(-1)` to see the contract trigger.
tips: Use `requires` for input validation - catches bugs at the call site
The Euclidean algorithm for GCD is efficient: O(log min(a,b))
Check primality only up to sqrt(n) - anything beyond that is redundant
common_mistakes: Using recursion for large inputs - iterative solutions avoid stack overflow
Not adding requires for functions that can't handle negative inputs
